start.text: The Slow Mercy noses up a channel no wider than she is, reeds hissing along both sides of her hull. Then the reeds open, and the water goes still.
Pools, everywhere, flat as poured glass. Each one holds a white sky and a reed and you, and none of them moves.
A plank staithe; a dyke going north to a hummock of reed houses; and far out on the mere, standing on four long legs in the fog, a lantern room with no light in it.
On every post of the staithe sits a little wooden gull, wings half open, all facing the same way: out, along the channel, toward the sea.
A woman in a grey shawl waits at the foot of the staithe, the way people wait for boats they didn't send for. She is looking at your hand.
